title: Local derived scalar cohomology depends only on the restricted derived object
statement: Let i:Y→X be any scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], R→S a morphism of commutative ring sheaves on X_proet, U an object of Y_proet, and K,K′ objects of D(R-modules). Use the actual completedAdicDerivedChange and sfbLocalRestriction of [def-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect-data]. A derived isomorphism sfbLocalRestriction i R U K ≅ sfbLocalRestriction i R U K′ induces an isomorphism between the underlying additive sheaves of H^q(S tensor^L_R K) and H^q(S tensor^L_R K′), after inverse image to Y and restriction to U, for every integer q. The map R→S is arbitrary; neither object has any boundedness, perfect-model or completeness hypothesis.

proof.text: Identify identity-coefficient ringed pullback with actual module inverse image by the identity scalar restriction unitor and uniqueness of left adjoints. Use exact-functor factors and localization representative isomorphisms to identify sfbLocalRestriction with the derived functor of module inverse image followed by slice restriction.

proof.text: Compare ordinary scalar extension with module inverse image by conjugating the commutative square of right adjoints: coefficient-unit naturality identifies restriction followed by pushforward with pushforward followed by restriction. Compare scalar extension with slice restriction by the identity on sectionwise pure tensors and the invertible slice/sheafification comparison. Adjunction uniqueness identifies the selected scalar-extension functors with these tensor constructions.

proof.text: Resolve each complex by a K-flat complex with flat terms. The algebraic inverse-image realization and the existing independent-coefficient inverse-image K-flat preservation lemma imply that module inverse image preserves K-flatness on this resolution class; transfer along its identifying functor isomorphism, then restrict to the slice, which retains K-flatness. The selected scalar-extension counits are invertible on these complexes. Descend the ordinary comparison, conjugated by these counits and the exact-functor factors, through the resolving-class localization to obtain a natural isomorphism of the two derived composites.

proof.text: Apply slice derived scalar extension to the given isomorphism and conjugate by the derived comparisons. Commute homology with the exact local module functor. Finally use the natural comparison of underlying additive sheaves with inverse image, followed by the definition of slice restriction, to obtain the stated isomorphism.

theorem proEtaleLocalScalarHomologyIso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Y ⟶ X)
    {R S : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1}} (φ : R ⟶ S)
    (U : Y.ProEt) (K K' : DerivedCategory (proEtaleRingModules X R))
    (e : sfbLocalRestriction i R U K ≅ sfbLocalRestriction i R U K') (q : ℤ) :
    Nonempty
      (((ProEt.topology Y).overPullback AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} U).obj
          ((proEtaleSheafInverseImage i AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
            ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf ((adicLisseForget X).obj S)).obj
              ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj
                ((completedAdicDerivedChange X φ).obj K)))) ≅
        ((ProEt.topology Y).overPullback AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} U).obj
          ((proEtaleSheafInverseImage i AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
            ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf ((adicLisseForget X).obj S)).obj
              ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj
                ((completedAdicDerivedChange X φ).obj K')))))
